minutes.headline: Bob Pease elected Conservation Commission chair as Richard Birch steps down; gazebo patio ordered removed.
minutes.summary: The remote Conservation Commission meeting handled several wetland hearings, including a field change at 150 Crossroad, approval of culvert replacement at Sunset Lane and Northfield Road, and a deck roof at 226 Sunset Lane with the gazebo patio ordered removed. It fined owners at 164 Bay Street and 9 Valley Road, issued a cease-and-desist at 99 Ruth Street, approved a conservation restriction, and elected new officers.

public_comment.topic: Thanked the outgoing chair and recommended Bob Pease as chair for the coming year.
Owner of the gazebo at 226 Sunset Lane said new owners should be told about wetland rules; unhappy at dismantling it.
Hickory Hills board member said the dock overlay misstates the channel and a larger dock would block it and sit near the neighbor.
Agreed with Waters; concerned a long dock would back up debris in heavy rain flows.
Abutter described erosion, ATV traffic, rope swing injury and new platform and stairs on the peninsula at 99 Ruth Street.

what_happened.line: The Commission ordered the gazebo patio at 226 Sunset Lane treated as a violation and removed, while approving the new deck on condition the gazebo area is restored.
Enforcement votes passed: fines for owners at 164 Bay Street and 9 Valley Road, and a cease-and-desist at 99 Ruth Street with an administrative hearing set.
The Commission approved the Notice of Intent for culvert replacement at Sunset Lane and Northfield Road.
It accepted a conservation restriction at 994 Northfield Road, contingent on the easement and subordination agreement.
Bob Pease was elected chair, with Ken Jones as vice chair and Carl Garlock as clerk.

why_it_matters: Wetland rulings decide what neighbors and property owners may build near wetlands, and the gazebo order and fines show unpermitted work can bring removal or penalties.
The culvert approval and the conservation restriction touch road drainage and protected land, both of which carry long-term upkeep and land-use effects in town.
watch_next: June 3rd at 7 p.m. by Zoom: continued hearings (3 Wilder, 47 Charlton Road), the Hickory Hills dock, and the 99 Ruth Street administrative hearing.
The signed, dated tree plan from the 150 Crossroad applicant, due by the next meeting.
